_doc: Stream E (play-test 2, Q18). Bespoke SET PIECES near the start (Torbor Fields, around Torborhold): hand-designed places bigger than a vignette, each with its own monsters, NPCs, quests (data/quests/setpieces.json; trainers in data/quests/classes.json), lore and chatter (data/names/chatter.json `place.<id>` + set-piece roles). A recipe is a vignette recipe (data/vignettes/README.md: props, monsters, objects — js/sim/vignettes.js reads it unchanged) PLUS: setpiece: true; kind; pin = where the placer puts it (zone; near = a settlement name or another set piece id; dist = [min, max] metres from its centre, fromEdge = from its circle edge; water = metres to water from the disc edge, waterSide = which local side faces it; road = within metres of a road; route = a route id from data/provinces/torbor_downs-routes.json; biome + biomeWithin; high = prefer high ground; awayFromRoad = at least metres off any road); ground = {flat, surface} for stream B (level the disc, paint it); parts = primitive boxes/cylinders/cones/domes ({mesh, x, z, y, w, h, d, colour, yaw}, the js/client/site-view.js part shape); models = named models ({id, x, z, yaw, scale}) that stream D-world builds in a reusable experiment — `models` below gives each a description and a primitive fallback (`parts`, local to the model origin) to draw until the real model exists; buildings = proctown building bodies by `want` ({want, x, z, w, d, yaw}); fields = crop plots ({x, z, w, d, yaw, crop}); folk = workers the placer turns into `folk` placements (role, work, chatter pools, local path); boss = an encounter id the placer stands at the centre (a `rare` placement with a short respawn). All coordinates local metres, +z = front (yaw 0), everything inside `radius`. PLAY-TEST 2 / stream B: `bind` = {zone, piece, name} puts this set piece's CONTENT (NPCs, monsters, objects, folk, props) onto stream B's baked ground piece of that id (data/world/set-pieces.json: B shapes the walls, fields, grave rows, buildings, pond); the placement record carries `bound` (the B piece id) and `scale` (B's radius / ours: stream A and D multiply recipe offsets by it), and a bound set piece's `models`/`parts`/`buildings`/`fields` are NOT drawn (B's piece has its own). `name: true` = the B piece takes our name (written to data/provinces/torbor_downs-places.json setPieces/lanes for B's bake).

gravestone.desc: An upright rounded-top headstone, ~1.1 m tall, weathered grey with lichen at the base; a few carved-name variants.

gravestone_leaning.desc: The same headstone tilted ~15 degrees and half sunk, moss on the low side.

tomb_chest.desc: A waist-high stone box tomb with a carved lid and a cracked corner.

iron_fence.desc: A 2 m section of black wrought-iron railing with spear-point finials, ~1.2 m tall; tiles end to end.

lychgate.desc: A roofed timber gateway into a churchyard: two posts, a small shingle roof, ~3 m wide, 3.2 m tall.

crypt_door.desc: A low stone ossuary front set into an earth bank: pitched stone lintel and a heavy iron-banded door.

scarecrow.desc: A cross of poles in a sack-head, ragged coat and straw hat, arms out, ~2.2 m.

haystack.desc: A rounded loose haystack about 2.5 m across with a pole through the top.

beehive.desc: A straw skep beehive on a little wooden stand; a few bees as particles.

cider_press.desc: A wooden screw press: a slatted tub, a big screw post and a turning bar, apple heap beside it.

apple_tree.desc: A short broad orchard apple tree, ~3.5 m, gnarled trunk, round crown with red fruit dots; a few windfalls.

watermill_wheel.desc: A 4.5 m undershot water wheel on an axle, wooden paddles, turning slowly; sits against the mill wall over the race.

millstone.desc: A pair of round grinding stones on a wooden frame, a grain hopper above.

sluice_gate.desc: A timber sluice: two posts and a sliding board with a lever, set across a channel.

hunters_tent.desc: A low A-frame hide tent, stained, guy ropes, a pelt over the door.

skinning_frame.desc: A rectangular pole frame with a stretched hide lashed inside it, knives on a stump beside.

trophy_post.desc: A tall post hung with antlers, skulls and a boar tusk necklace; the hunters' boast board.

smoking_rack.desc: A smoke-blackened pole rack over a smouldering pit, strips of meat and fish hanging.

standing_stone.desc: A rough grey megalith 2.5-3.5 m tall, lichen-spotted, slightly tapered; variants by scale and lean.

altar_stone.desc: A flat recumbent slab on two low stones, worn hollow in the middle.

shrine_statue.desc: A 2.2 m stone figure of a hooded mother holding a bowl to her chest, on a plinth, worn smooth by hands.

offering_bowl.desc: A shallow stone bowl on a short pillar, coins and flowers in it.

prayer_cairn.desc: A knee-high heap of flat painted pebbles, each with a scratched wish.

broken_tower.desc: The stump of a round stone tower, 6-7 m, the top bitten off, scorched, one empty window.

collapsed_stair.desc: A stone stair climbing a broken wall to nowhere, the top steps fallen into rubble.

sigil_slab.desc: A cracked floor slab carved with a ring of unreadable marks that faintly glow violet at night.

saw_pit.desc: A long rectangular pit with a log on trestles across it and a two-man saw; sawdust heap.

log_stack.desc: A neat pyramid of felled trunks, bark on, ~4 m long, chocked with wedges.

grindstone.desc: A round whetstone wheel in a wooden frame with a foot treadle and a water trough.

tree_stump.desc: A fresh-cut stump, pale top, axe left in it sometimes.

jetty.desc: A plank jetty on posts, 6 m long and 1.6 m wide, running out over the water.

rowboat.desc: A small clinker rowboat, oars shipped, pulled up or moored.

fish_trap.desc: A wicker funnel fish trap on a rope, some stacked on the bank.

rod_rack.desc: A lean-to rack holding four fishing rods and a coil of net.

inn_sign.desc: A painted hanging sign on a gallows post: a milk pail over a plough.

hitching_post.desc: A horizontal rail on two posts with an iron ring, for tying horses.

bench.desc: A rough plank bench for two.

notice_post.desc: A board on a post with layered nailed notices (bounties, lost sheep).

training_dummy.desc: A straw-stuffed sack man on a post, arms of rope, battered shield; spins a little when hit.

archery_butt.desc: A round straw target with painted rings on an A-frame stand, arrows stuck in it.

weapon_rack.desc: A wooden rack of blunt practice swords, staves and spears.

sand_pit.desc: A shallow ring of raked sand edged with half-buried logs, 6 m across, for sparring.

bone_heap.desc: A knee-high heap of gnawed sheep and deer bones, a few collars and a boot.

den_mouth.desc: A low earth-and-root overhang hollow, big enough for a horse-sized hound, darkness inside, bones at the lip.

grave_mound.desc: A fresh rounded earth mound with a wooden marker, 2 m long.

open_grave.desc: A dug grave pit with spoil heaped beside it and a spade stuck in.

bell_frame.desc: A small bell hung in a two-post timber frame with a pull rope (the sexton's bell).

gear_housing.desc: A wooden casing with a big wooden cog wheel visible through a missing plank.

wooden_fence.desc: A 3 m section of split-rail field fence, two rails on three posts.

stone_wall.desc: A 3 m stretch of dry-stone wall, knee-to-waist high, uneven top.

vignettes.name: Torbor Drill Field
vignettes.blurb: The town watch's practice ground just outside Torborhold: straw dummies, archery butts, a sand sparring pit and racks of blunt weapons. Sergeant-at-Arms (trainer_arms) trains warriors, fighters, knights, swashbucklers, dragon knights and tacticians here; their class quests start here. Safe, no monsters.
vignettes.lore: Straw men with a hundred dents in them, a ring of raked sand, and a rack of swords too blunt to hurt anyone but your pride.

objects.name: Straw dummy
objects.text: You lay into the dummy until straw flies. Your arms recall how this is done.

objects.name: Archery butts
objects.text: You pull three arrows out of the outer ring and one out of the fence. Nobody saw. Probably.

objects.name: Weapon rack
objects.text: Blunt blades, warped staves, a spear with a sock tied to the point. Practice gear, but honest.

objects.name: Sand pit
objects.text: You walk the ring once. The sand still holds the shape of somebody falling hard.

objects.name: Drill roster
objects.text: DRILL — dawn, every day but feast days. Bring your own bandages. The sergeant does not do bandages. — B.H.

vignettes.name: Brannock Fields
vignettes.blurb: A working farm just outside Torborhold: a farmhouse and barn, a wheat field, a turnip patch, a cabbage strip, an apple orchard with beehives and a cider press. Two boars raid the turnips. Quests from Hesketh Brannock (scarecrow, boars) and Ada the orchard keeper (cider). Folk: two farmers, an orchard keeper.
vignettes.lore: Wheat to your knees, apples overhead, and a scarecrow that has clearly seen things.

objects.name: Scarecrow
objects.text: The scarecrow's button eyes follow you. You straighten its hat. It seems grateful, which is worse.

objects.name: Cider press
objects.text: You give the screw a turn. A trickle of cloudy cider comes out. It is very strong.

objects.name: Beehives
objects.text: You lift a lid. The bees discuss you, loudly. You put the lid back.

objects.name: Planting tally
objects.text: Wheat in the long field. Turnips by the ditch (fence them, Hesketh, I mean it). Cabbages where the old pig sty was. Apples will do what apples do.

objects.name: Hidden seed jar
objects.hint: Farmers hide the good seed where nobody looks: under the step of the farmhouse.

vignettes.name: Turnwater Mill
vignettes.blurb: A stone watermill on a stream (the water is behind it, local -z): the wheel, a sluice, the millstones under an open shed, a grain store at +x where cairn rats breed. The mill-wright (trainer_tinker) trains tinkers here. Quests from Miller Hob Turnwater (rats; the sluice).
vignettes.lore: The wheel groans round, the stones grumble, and somewhere in the grain sacks something squeaks back.

objects.name: Millstone
objects.text: You sweep the stones. The flour is gritty — someone has been grinding more than grain. Rat droppings, mostly.

objects.name: Sluice lever
objects.text: You heave the lever. The race roars, the wheel picks up speed, and the whole mill shudders awake.

objects.name: Gear housing
objects.text: Through a gap you see the great cog. Three teeth are new oak, carved by someone very patient.

objects.name: Mill ledger
objects.text: Sacks in: 40. Sacks out: 31. Rats: yes. Also one sack of something that was not grain. Ask nobody.

vignettes.name: Saint Hulda's Yard
vignettes.blurb: Torborhold's old churchyard: an iron-railed square, a lychgate at the front (+z), four rows of graves either side of a stone path, box tombs, a fresh open grave in the back-right corner, and an ossuary dug into the back bank between the ruined chapel walls. Two barrow hounds dig among the graves. Old Mother Quell (trainer_grave) trains necromancers here. Quests from Sexton Abel Fenn (the hounds; the bell and the grave dust). One lantern (torch post) at the gate, nothing else lit.
vignettes.lore: The railings lean in as if listening. Somebody has dug a grave very recently, and somebody else has been digging the other way.

objects.name: Sexton's bell
objects.text: You ring it once. Every crow in the yard leaves. Something under the ground goes very still.

objects.name: Open grave
objects.text: Six feet down, as is proper. The coffin lid is cracked — from the inside? No. Surely not.

objects.name: Ossuary door
objects.text: The iron door is cold enough to sting. Behind it, bones are stacked by size, as tidy as firewood.

objects.name: Weathered epitaph
objects.text: HERE LIES WAT THATCHER. HE SAID THE ROOF WOULD HOLD.

objects.name: Grave goods
objects.hint: Someone was buried with their purse. The box tomb in the back-right corner does not quite close.

vignettes.name: Greyfletch Camp
vignettes.blurb: The Greyfletch family's hunting camp at the edge of the woods: hide tents round a fire, a skinning frame, smoking rack, a trophy post of antlers and a tally board of kills. Huntmaster Oswy Greyfletch (trainer_hunt) trains rangers, witch hunters and demon hunters and gives the start chain's mini-boss branch (Old Gristle). Two hunters about camp. Safe.
vignettes.lore: Smoke, drying meat and the smell of wet dog. Antlers on a post, and a board with tally marks for everything that ever walked past.

objects.name: Skinning frame
objects.text: A moor hound pelt the size of a cart cover is stretched here. The hunters say the beast it came from was the small one.

objects.name: Trophy post
objects.text: Antlers, tusks, a boar's jaw — and a bare nail with a name scratched under it: GRISTLE. Waiting.

objects.name: Tally board
objects.text: Columns of tally marks: hounds, boars, croakers. One column is headed "fools who went alone". It is long.

objects.name: Smoking rack
objects.text: You help yourself to a strip of smoked venison. Nobody stops you, which means it is the bad batch.

vignettes.name: Gristle's Hollow
vignettes.blurb: The lair of Old Gristle (mb_old_gristle), the huge moor hound that leads the packs into the sheep folds: an earth overhang den at the back (-z), bones and collars everywhere, two of his hounds lounging. The placer puts the boss at the centre (`boss`). Start chain branch B ends here. No NPCs.
vignettes.lore: Bones. Old ones, new ones, sheep ones, and a few you would rather not identify. The den mouth breathes out warm air.

objects.name: Gnawed collar
objects.text: A shepherd's dog collar, chewed through. The brass tag reads: BESS. GOOD GIRL. COME HOME.

objects.name: Bone heap
objects.text: You turn over the heap. Sheep, deer, a boar skull cracked like a nut. Whatever eats here is very big and very sure of itself.

vignettes.name: The Nine Maidens
vignettes.blurb: A ring of nine standing stones on high ground with a heel stone outside the ring (+z) and a recumbent altar at the centre; a fairy ring of mushrooms. Wenna of the Stones (trainer_wilds) trains druids and shamans here. Quests from Bettony the herb-woman (mushrooms; the heel stone at dusk). Safe.
vignettes.lore: Nine stones, dancing in a ring, caught mid-step a very long time ago. The wind sounds different inside.

objects.name: Heel stone
objects.text: You lay a palm on the heel stone. For a heartbeat the ring seems to turn, and you are standing still in the middle of it.

objects.name: Altar stone
objects.text: The hollow in the altar is full of rainwater that does not ripple when you breathe on it.

objects.name: Ring of mushrooms
objects.text: You step over the ring, not into it. Everybody knows that much.

vignettes.name: Shrine of the Kind Mother
vignettes.blurb: A small roadside shrine: a worn statue of a hooded mother holding a bowl, an offering bowl full of coins and flowers, prayer cairns of painted pebbles, a stone bench. Brother Cadoc (trainer_mind) trains monks and oracles here. Quest from Pilgrim Orla (lost prayer stones). No lights, no monsters.
vignettes.lore: A stone mother with a bowl, her face worn smooth by a thousand hands. The flowers in the bowl are fresh.

objects.name: Offering bowl
objects.text: The coin sinks among the others with a soft chink. Something tight in your chest loosens.

objects.name: Prayer stones
objects.text: Each pebble carries a scratched wish: "rain", "no rain", "let him come back", "let him NOT come back".

objects.name: Mother's statue
objects.text: You touch the worn hands like everyone else has. They are warm, though the morning is not.

vignettes.name: Coldharrow Ruins
vignettes.blurb: The burned shell of Coldharrow manor and the stump of its tower: roofless walls, an arch, a collapsed stair, a cracked floor sigil that glows faintly at night. Road brigands squat by a fire on the east side. Ysolde Coldharrow, last of the family (trainer_pact), trains warlocks here and is the reason the house burned. Quests from Warden Maddoc (the brigands; how the fire started).
vignettes.lore: The fire was thirty years ago and the stones still smell of it. In the middle of the old hall, the floor is cracked in a perfect circle.

objects.name: Cracked sigil
objects.text: Your shadow falls across the circle and, for a moment, keeps going without you. Then it comes back.

objects.name: Collapsed stair
objects.text: The stair climbs to a doorway that opens on thirty feet of air. Scorch marks lead up, and none lead down.

objects.name: Burnt letter
objects.text: ...the circle is drawn, Father. You said we had no gift. Watch. — Y.  (The rest is ash.)

objects.name: Buried strongbox
objects.hint: Old houses hid their silver under the hearth. Find where the great fireplace stood, west end of the hall.

vignettes.name: Ashby's Lumber Camp
vignettes.blurb: A clearing hacked into the forest edge: stumps everywhere at the back, a saw pit with a log across it, stacked trunks, a grindstone, a foreman's hut and a cook fire. Dusk flitters roost in the cut timber. Quests from Foreman Edda Ashby (flitters; a missing saw). Folk: two woodcutters and the foreman.
vignettes.lore: Sawdust, sap and swearing. The forest stops here in a hard line of stumps, like a crowd that stepped back from something.

objects.name: Saw pit
objects.text: You take the bottom of the saw for a dozen strokes and get a face full of sawdust for your trouble. Honest work.

objects.name: Log pile
objects.text: The top log has claw marks along it. Not axe marks. Claw marks, and something has been sleeping in the gaps.

objects.name: Grindstone
objects.text: You pump the treadle and put an edge back on your blade. The stone sings.

vignettes.name: Tench Pool
vignettes.blurb: A quiet fishing spot: a plank jetty out over the water (local -z), a moored rowboat, wicker fish traps, a rod rack under a lean-to and a smoking fire. Fen croakers squat in the reeds and steal the catch. Quest from Old Wat the fisher (croakers; the big tench). Folk: one fisher.
vignettes.lore: Still water, a sagging jetty and a fisher who has not caught anything since the croakers moved in.

objects.name: Rod rack
objects.text: You borrow a rod and cast. Something takes the bait, considers you, and lets go.

objects.name: Fish traps
objects.text: You haul a trap. Empty — but the wicker is bitten clean through. Croakers, or something with a better jaw.

objects.name: Old jetty
objects.text: You sit at the end of the jetty with your feet over the water. The pool is very deep and very calm. You feel rested.

vignettes.name: The Pail and Plough
vignettes.blurb: A crossroads inn on the Torborhold–Orrinsford road, halfway: the inn (front to the road, +z), a stable, a well, benches and a long table outside, hitching posts, a signpost and a notice post. Innkeeper Marra (innkeeper_marra, start chain hub: both branches open here). Lute-master Emrys Fenwick (trainer_bard) trains bards here. A safe stop: no monsters. Lit (torches at the door and the yard).
vignettes.lore: A painted sign of a milk pail over a plough, a stable that smells of hay, and the noise of somebody losing at dice indoors.

objects.name: Inn sign
objects.text: A milk pail over a plough, freshly repainted. The pail has been given a face. The face looks worried.

objects.name: Well
objects.text: Cold, sweet water. You drink deep and the road dust goes down with it.

objects.name: Notice post
objects.text: LOST: one ox, answers to Duchess. FOUND: one ox, answers to nothing. REWARD for news of the big hound on the south road.

objects.name: Hearth
objects.text: Through the open door you warm your hands at the great hearth. Somebody hands you a bowl of something brown and hot without asking. Bliss.
